f.d: User profile subschemas The profile object for a user is defined by a composite schema of base and custom properties using a JSON path to r…
All Okta-defined profile properties are defined in a profile subschema with the resolution scope `#base`.
The `#base` object properties
City or locality component of the user's address (`locality`)
Name of a cost center assigned to the user
Country name component of the user's address (`country`.) This property uses ISO 3166-1 alpha 2 "short" code format.
Name of the user's department
Name of the user, suitable for display to end users
Name of the user's division
Primary email address of the user.
Organization or company assigned unique identifier for the user
Given name of the user (`givenName`)
Honorific prefix(es) of the user or title in most Western languages
Honorific suffix(es) of the user
Family name of the user (`familyName`)
User's default location for purposes of localizing items such as currency, date time format, numerical representations, and so on.
Unique identifier for the user (`userName`) The login property is validated according to its pattern attribute, which is a string.
The `displayName` of the user's manager
The `id` of the user's manager
Middle name(s) of the user
Mobile phone number of the user
Casual way to address the user in real life
Name of the user's organization
Mailing address component of the user's address
User's preferred written or spoken languages.
Primary phone number of the user, such as home number
URL of the user's online profile (for example, a web page.) This property is formatted according to the Relative Uniform Resource Locators…
Secondary email address of the user typically used for account recovery.
State or region component of the user's address (`region`)
Full street address component of the user's address
User's time zone.
User's title, such as "Vice President"
Used to describe the organization to the user relationship such as "Employee" or "Contractor".
ZIP code or postal code component of the user's address (`postalCode`)
